chapter: Band building and learning from musicians
title: Getting along in a band; Albert Warner and Sonny Henry
summary: DeVore says a band with bad feeling cannot play well, and mentions the unspoken closeness of Albert Warner and Sonny Henry.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Oh absolutely. Yeah. Not only from the musical and from the philosophy and that's just as important as anything else. I mean being able to get along with your fellow man that seems to be the most important thing of all. When there's a bad feeling running in the band you're not going to play as good music. I found that out from bitter experience. So no matter how good a guy is and if you're not getting along you're not going to be able to come up with a real New Orleans feeling. Very, very few bands would be able to overcome the personal conflict angle. The bands that were able to overcome were the ones that stuck together the longest and played probably the best collective improvisation.
There's a philosophy of playing in a band and understanding
and understanding who you are in relation to the other people. At least to me it seems to me. Even though it's never spoken sometimes.
talking about Albert Warner and Sonny Henry. Crazy. You say, you guys good buddies? They probably say, oh, I don't know, he's kind of a no good SOB. Kidding me. But you knew that they were always

bummed together. Sure. And that's just as those two things from a strictly musical angle and from a strictly getting along angle. Very important. As anybody who's ever played in a jazz band can tell you. Well, say
